query: High-entropy alloys contain five or more elements at 5–35 at% each, generally with comparable atomic radii. Refractory and nickel-based high-entropy alloys have demonstrated elevated-temperature mechanical properties comparable to titanium- and nickel-based alloys used in extreme environments because of their heat resistance and specific strength. However, prior investigations have mainly treated titanium and nickel as additions, leaving alloys in which both are primary constituents unexplored. Subject to the stated compositional definition, what single testable intervention hypothesis could improve the elevated-temperature mechanical properties of a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy relative to the same material without the intervention? Specify the intervention, causal mechanism, predicted relative outcome, composition and operating boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of 5 at. pct. Ti to a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy will improve its elevated-temperature mechanical properties through precipitation hardening.
generation.baseline: Titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy without Ti addition
generation.boundary: Composition: 5 at. pct. Ti, Temperature: elevated
generation.uncertainty: The effect of Ti addition on the microstructure and properties of the alloy at elevated temperatures is not fully understood

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the elevated-temperature mechanical properties of titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloys with and without 5 at. pct. Ti addition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy with Ti addition does not show improved elevated-temperature mechanical properties compared to the alloy without Ti addition, the hypothesis is falsified

## Abstract
AbstractThe effect of Al and Ti additions on the microstructure and properties of CoNiFe alloys was studied in this paper. The investigations were conducted on four specially designed and produced arc furnace alloys (from 3 to 5 components, with medium to high entropy). Samples in various states were analyzed, i.e., as-cast, after homogenization, after solution heat treatment, and after solution heat treatment and aging. The obtained samples were characterized by: SEM observations, EDS, XRD, TEM analyses, and finally, hardness measurements. The solid solution strengthening coming from the addition of 5 at. pct. Al was negligible, while the effect from the 5 at. pct. of Ti addition was significant. The precipitation hardening effect related to the presence of the (CoNi)3Ti phase caused by the Ti addition is comparable with the total effect of the Al and Ti addition, which caused the precipitation of (NiCo)3AlTi.Keywords: high-entropy alloys, heat treatment, aging, microstructure, mechanical properties
